brief.headline: Indian Equities Face Tariff and Inflation Headwinds as Crude Surges
brief.summary: Indian markets open under pressure following a jump in Brent crude above $95 per barrel and proposed US tariffs. IT stocks remain exposed to rupee movements while bond yields climb on RBI inflation commentary.

takeaways.text: Indian government bonds tumble as Brent crude tops $95 per barrel and the RBI flags mounting food inflation risks.
The rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 against the dollar in early trade, driven by higher crude prices and tariff concerns.
US proposes extra tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, dropping to 17% if a trade deal is signed.
European stocks rally as tech and bank shares rebound, while US GDP growth figures keep December rate hikes in play.
Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia under strict export controls, while S&P considers a credit downgrade.

sections.india: Indian government bonds fell sharply as Brent crude surpassed $95 per barrel, with the Reserve Bank of India highlighting persistent food inflation pressures. The rupee dropped 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade amid higher oil prices and proposed US tariffs. Meanwhile, corporate developments saw Adani entities plan public bond sales to raise at least Rs 20 billion, and Tata Trusts move to challenge N Chandrasekaran's reappointment at Tata Sons.
sections.world: European equities rallied as technology and bank stocks rebounded and tariff fears temporarily eased. In the US, revised third-quarter GDP figures showing 4.3% growth kept December interest rate hike expectations alive for the Federal Reserve. Concurrently, China hit back against fresh US tariff threats, injecting new trade tensions into global markets ahead of scheduled meetings.
sections.tech: Nvidia halted chip shipments to south-east Asia to comply with tightening US export controls aimed at restricting Chinese access to advanced AI computing power. S&P considered a credit downgrade for Nvidia to AA- citing governance and key man risks. Meanwhile, SpaceX secured FCC approval to deploy up to 1 million orbital compute modules for orbital data centres.
